fields.statement: At 6b5628b I built rhiza into a scratch dir and ran `rhiza run start <record> --workflow plan --autonomous` in a scratch repo against real Rex, in a dedicated Rex session. A caller-side rex shim forwarded every call to the real rex and only pointed new panes at a fake claude that stays alive after `rhiza session done`, as Claude Code does. Real Rex got exactly one `window new` (interview). The review session split the interview's live block, the critic split the review's block, and all five session records share one window. Panes left open by `until held` stayed alive. When the interview window had been emptied (an agent that exits on its own), the next step correctly fell back to `window new`. The named Go tests and testscripts also pass.

Same real-Rex autonomous plan run at 6b5628b. The planner asked two questions through the real PreToolUse hook. Each arbiter session opened with `rex split` of the planner's block, the second after the first arbiter's closed block failed as anchor and Rhiza split a live pane of the window instead. Neither arbiter opened a window, and the run succeeded with assume-1 and assume-2 landed. In a normal `ask` workflow run on real Rex, the advisor session for the owner question split the asking session's block in the run's one window, and rhiza inbox showed the recommendation.

On real Rex at 6b5628b, with fake agents that keep running after `session done`: each arbiter's journal had `arbitrated` (08:57:41.99Z), then rhiza issued `rex block close` of the arbiter's block, then sent the answer to the asker (`answered` 08:57:42.09Z). The arbiter block vanished from `rex block ls` within a second, killing its still-running agent, while the interview, review and critic panes stayed open. For the advisor, `recommended` was journalled at 09:01:22.018Z and `rex block close` of the advisor's block followed at once. The pane and its process were gone within a second, while the asker's pane stayed open. A first advisor run whose pane PATH lacked rex left the pane open (no close), confirming the close comes from run recommend.
